rationale: Both candidates independently surface the ground truth's implicit scope-creep concern (widening past CUDA/MUSA to any non-CPU device, echoing yeahdongcn's defensive clarification) and both partially touch the device_module/platform-binding concern gcanlin raised, while both miss the actual resolution (dropping the redundant VAE unit test since E2E covers it) by arguing for more tests instead. X goes further with a rigorously verified, source-level catch that `fork_rng`'s `device_type` param still defaults to "cuda" so the seeding fix silently forks/restores the wrong device's RNG state — a genuinely serious, well-grounded bug Y never finds, which also undercuts Y's more lenient 'approve' verdict given the same NPU/scope evidence Y itself surfaced. Both reviews are concrete and actionable with file/line citations and code fixes, but X's added depth and internal consistency (verdict matches severity of findings) give it the edge.
